title: Essentially smooth ring maps
statement: A homomorphism of commutative rings $R\to D$ is *essentially smooth* if there are a smooth $R$-algebra $P$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] and a multiplicative subset $S\subset P$ such that $D\cong S^{-1}P$ as $R$-algebras. (Every smooth, in particular every étale, ring map is essentially smooth, with $S=\{1\}$; if $D$ is local one may take $S=P\setminus\mathfrak P$ for a prime $\mathfrak P$ of $P$.)

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Section 07FF (section-inseparable): the term 'essentially smooth' is used without definition in Lemmas 07FH (lemma-solution-modulo, line 2571: 'the first arrow is essentially smooth'), 07FI (lemma-enlarge-solution-modulo, line 2638) and the proof of Lemma 07FJ (lines 2727, 2752, 3064); the definition here (a localization of a smooth algebra, modelled on 'essentially of finite type' = localization of a finite type algebra, Algebra, Definition Tag 00QM, algebra-definition-essentially-finite-p-t) is written by an agent
